name: News Corporation
sector: Media / Publishing, professional data & digital real estate
moat_justification: Two genuine franchises inside a conglomerate: Dow Jones (brand, 6.26M digital-only subs, Risk & Compliance/Energy B2B data with switching costs) and REA Group's Australian portal network effects, plus HarperCollins scale. But the moat is blended, not consolidated: News Media (~$2.23B revenue) earns near-zero segment EBITDA, and consolidated ROE ran only 1.8–7.6% in FY22–26 excluding FY25's Foxtel-gain year (fundamentals.json; the roic_proxy and gross-margin series are null because News Corp tags no operating-income/COGS lines the engine can use). Returns below the cost of capital through the cycle cap this at moderate — 5/10.
fragility_flags: NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Diversified media conglomerate — two real franchises (Dow Jones, REA/Realtor.com) diluted by a near-zero-profit News Media segment, moat 5/10 — at $32.83 the consolidated owner's earnings support only a 7.2% weighted IRR (weighted IV@15% $11.73); it clears 15% only below ~$11.73.
moat_for: Dow Jones: WSJ/Barron's brands with 6.26M digital-only subscriptions and a growing enterprise/B2B recurring base
Professional Information Business: Risk & Compliance revenue $392M in FY26 (+16%) and Dow Jones Energy — data products with real switching costs
REA Group: Australia's dominant property portal with network effects (146.4M average monthly visits in FY26)
HarperCollins: Big Five scale and a deep backlist, with audiobooks/e-books growing double digits
Net-cash balance sheet (net debt -$106M) and $641M of FY26 buybacks shrinking the share count
moat_against: News Media (~$2.23B FY26 revenue) earns near-zero segment EBITDA — structural print decline drags consolidated returns
Consolidated ROE only 1.8–7.6% across FY22–26 excluding the Foxtel-gain year — returns below the cost of capital through the cycle
Realtor.com is No. 2 to Zillow in the US and housing-cycle exposed
Book publishing is hit-driven and platform-dependent (Amazon, Audible/Spotify); AI content licensing is opportunistic, not a contracted moat
Dual-class Murdoch control and a persistent conglomerate discount; the segments do not reinforce each other
